questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I really wanted to go to Japan as I think the country is fascinating, great food culture, nature, etc. I did not know a lot about the academic level but I had a good impression of the university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was an incredible time. I loved living in Japan. People were nice, food was great, city and nature was great. The university was a good experience as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as the university was incredible helpful. If i write an email I would get an answer within a few hours. It was also a possibility to call the international office and they would help with litterally anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mentioned, very easy to email them. Furthermore, there was an orientation day which was fine. I didn't live in student acommodation so I didn't go to the main campus (Tama) that much, but they also had an office there. We also had a small orientation day at Myogadani Campus where I took my courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite okay. My girlfriend was also on exchange so that helped as we could look at apartments together. But there are many options to rent a room through sites such as Sakura House.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You are of course a bit disconnected from the campus life and many exchange students choose the student housing. However, I really enjoyed living in the city. The housing offered by uni is far away. I loved being close to everything in Tokyo and the apartment I lived in was just 15 minutes from Myogadani Campus - very convenient.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing was fine in terms of quality and price. Unfortunately, the housing was very far away from the city and also from Myogadani Campus where I took my courses.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register for courses before the semester started, but then we had the possibility to change courses within two weeks if I remember correctly. The courses/study plan had to be "approved" my my academic advisor. He didn't seem to care that much so I cannot imagine they will not accept the courses you choose.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Email service with the international office who spoke English. There was also an office in Myogadani Campus, but they did not really speak English. You can still do it with Google Translate and everyone do everything they can to help even though they do not speak English

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of them. There are very few courses to take in English though. Especially in political science so I had to choose law courses

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the international office for assistance if you have any questions. They help with everything - I have never received so efficient and helpful advice and assistance before, incredible! Be aware there are not that many English courses to take.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I enjoyed my courses overall. However, as mentioned, very few courses in English. Sometimes the level isn't the highest as not everyone speaks English that well while some teachers did not always prepare that well. One course was bad, but we voiced our concerns to the university and they listened and took action.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took MA courses but also BA as I had to take 6 courses due to Japanese visa rules. there were really few, relevant MA courses unfortunately. The BA courses were audit courses. The level was varying, but overall fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More presentation, you have to be more active. Less reading. Lower level. Nice and listening teachers willing to help and also adjust the teaching after your preferences.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Human RIghts in a Globalized World
Law and Society
Public Governance
Ethics and Humanitarian Intervention
Global Tutorial

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend Public governance and Law and Society. Nice and capable teachers, very interesting topics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I used the trains/metros etc. a lot which got quite expensive. The Shinkansen is also extremely expensive. There is also an obligatory Japanese insurance, but it wasn't that expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was incredible and quite cheap! I ate out every day and it wasn't that bad financially. People talk as if Tokyo is incredibly expensive but I found it very reasonable, especially compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined a hiking club and there were several other clubs. It can be quite difficult to join if you do not speak English though.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Hiking, sports, dancing, manga, etc.: lots of clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Food, Izakaya, hiking, enjoying living in TOkyo

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Several nice day trips such as going to Hakone. Hiking Mt Fuji was also a great experience. Okinawa was beautiful and fascinating. Museums are good. You can do pretty much everything in Japan :-). There are also several food, music, etc. festivals in the spring and summer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. Of course it was difficult not speaking Japanese as many do not speak English. But people were helpful, you always felt safe. Also, I got several Japanese friends at university who were open and nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to the Japanese students you take classes with. I experienced that many were interested and wanted to learn English and they were always kind if you say hi. Also, you can join clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food, the incredible hospitality. Everyone was nice and helpful. The university staff as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn a few phrases of Japanes or download Google Translate (use the picture translating feature!)

Read up on which courses are available as there are only few courses available

Enjoy the amazing experience! It is an amazing privilege to be able to live in Tokyo and Japan and go on exchange in general.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Try to engage with Japanese students you take classes with. They can help show you all the best food places, etc. I was not that engaged in the exchange students environment but everyone seemed nice.

Take advantage of the incredible help Chuo University provides. They go to great lengths to help and be kind to you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new friends, eating great food, learning about the Japanese society and getting new perspectives on my own studies. Traveling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
